newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo bourse peaks on last 1996 market day.
newsitem.headline: Oslo bourse peaks on last 1996 market day.

text.p: Last-minute window-dressing and investment in blue chips lifted Norwegian shares to the 55th record closing high of 1996 on the last market day on Monday.

Oslo's Total index finished 0.84 percent higher at 968.37 in healthy trade worth 774 million crowns. Dealers said foreign investors were buying blue chip stock anticipating rising share prices in Oslo in January. The index climbed 32 percent in 1996.
"It will continue to rise in January because interest rates are low and the economy so strong there won't be many disappointments when the companies present the annual results," one analyst said.
"But U.S. developments will continue to have a major influence on the Oslo Bourse," he cautioned.
A dealer said: "Today was mostly window-dressing and also mutual funds."
Small-time savers are paying into mutual funds in late December to carry tax breaks into January.
Norsk Hydro rose 1.76 percent to 346 crowns, Orkla B shares were up 1.51 percent at 404 crowns and Kvaerner A stock gained 1.64 percent to finish at 310.50 crowns.
Norsk Hydro, which has a 20 percent weighting on the Total index, was the most traded share at 95.6 million crowns.
